subject: Cross-cloud go-to-market: joint marketplace listing plan and region/SKU split
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@amazon.com>
Cc: Guneet Singh <g.singh@azurepartnerships.microsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-cloud go-to-market: joint marketplace listing plan and region/SKU split

Team / partners,

Thanks for the calls this week — following up with a single thread to lock down which SKUs we list on each cloud and the regional packaging approach for the VectorRetail pilot. Goal: have a minimal set of production listings (SKU + packaging) per cloud by end of month so VectorRetail can launch with co-sell support.

Proposed agenda / asks:
- Confirm recommended SKU set per cloud (core, performance, enterprise) — see attached sku-matrix-v1.xlsx.
- Decide regional prioritization for canary (US East, EU West) and fallback regions.
- Identify cloud-specific packaging requirements (metering, support tiers, billing model).
- Clarify co-sell eligibility checklist per partner and intake links.

Samantha / Guneet, can you confirm the minimum marketplace requirements for co-sell eligibility on AWS/Azure/GCP respectively? We want to avoid rework when we submit listings.

I attached the initial SKU matrix. Marissa + Ben: please annotate with recommended default pricing and any compliance packaging notes (EU data residency). Karthik: can you validate whether Dedicated / Private variants should be separate SKUs or options on the same listing?

Proposed next step: 30m sync Tue 13 Jan 10:00 PT to finalize choices — I’ll send calendar if that works.

Thanks,

— Priyom Das
Senior GTM Manager
Redwood Inference
(priyom_das@redwood.ai)

Attachments: sku-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet outlining candidate SKUs and variant columns)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@amazon.com>
Cc: Guneet Singh <g.singh@azurepartnerships.microsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud go-to-market: joint marketplace listing plan and region/SKU split

Thanks Priyom — quick pass on the matrix attached. High-level thoughts:

- SKU naming: suggest "Core", "Core+", "Enterprise" as canonical SKUs across clouds and then an optional "Dedicated" add-on managed as a configurable product option where the cloud supports it. Keeps listings simpler and reduces friction in marketplace forms.
- Pricing: draft price bands in attached pricing-proposal-draft.pdf — two notes: 1) AWS and GCP prefer per-hour or per-vCPU metering for compute-heavy services; Azure favors a monthly metered plan for ISV co-sell flows.
- Regions: recommend US East for initial canary, EU West for GDPR-sensitive customers (VectorRetail specifically needs EU coverage). APAC can be staged later; don't block launch.
- Compliance packaging: for EU customers we should have a separate "EU Data Plan" checkbox on the listing that references the Private offering (on-prem/VPC) and points to our KMS/HSM page.

I attached pricing-proposal-draft.pdf and added inline comments in the drive link. For the Tue sync: works for me at 10:00 PT.

— Marissa
Director, GTM Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-proposal-draft.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 08:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud go-to-market: joint marketplace listing plan and region/SKU split

+1 on Marissa. A few ops-level constraints I want captured before we submit:

- Marketplace listing cadence: AWS takes ~2–4 weeks for technical & commercial review for new ISV listings; Azure can be faster if the co-sell motion is pre-engaged by the partner team. Factor that into our timeline.
- SKU variants: prefer a single listing with variant attributes rather than multiple full SKUs for the same product (reduces bookkeeping). If a cloud forces separate SKUs for Dedicated, we'll accept that but mark as "dependency" in the intake.
- Support tiers: marketplace listing must map to our support SLAs — add the "Marketplace listing checklist" doc (attached) for the intake owner so we don't miss security artifacts.

On the matrix: I flagged fields where we need partner IDs, publisher account numbers, and exact billing model choices. Priyom — please consolidate those on the call and we can assign the intake owner.

Ben Carter
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-cloud go-to-market: joint marketplace listing plan and region/SKU split

Hi all — great summary, thanks for pulling this together. A few AWS-specific notes from the ISV/Marketplace side:

- Co-sell eligibility (AWS): you need a validated listing, go-to-market plan, and an assigned AWS Partner SA/Account team. The AWS intake form we use is here: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/partners/intake. Please complete the commercial worksheet and upload the sku-matrix there.
- SKU design: AWS supports product variants but many partners choose single listing + optional add-ons. Per-hour or per-instance metering is common for inference workloads.
- Regional availability: we can syndicate a global listing but you should have a documented fallback for EU data residency — AWS will require clear language in the listing if a customer requires EU-only hosting.
- Docs: include a short architecture diagram, an SLA summary, and a security checklist (SOC2/ISO).

I can help fast-track reviews if we have the commercial worksheet and the DocuSign MSA (link suggested). Also recommended: schedule a 30m intake review with our listing ops on Tue 20 Jan — I can coordinate if you share preferred times.

Samantha Lee
Marketplace Partner Manager, AWS ISV
Samantha.Lee@amazon.com

Thanks everyone — quick recap and actions from the sync: 

- Confirmed SKUs: Core, Core+, Enterprise + optional Dedicated add-on (as Marissa suggested).
- Canaries: US East (primary), EU West (privacy-sensitive fallback). APAC staged later.
- Owner assignments: Priyom (intake coordination & DocuSign MSA), Marissa (pricing approvals), Ben (marketplace ops checklist & submission owner), Karthik (technical packaging / Dedicated variant feasibility).
- External asks: Samantha to share the AWS commercial worksheet link (she included above) and available intake review times. Guneet / Marco — please confirm any Azure/GCP special fields we should populate (billing model, publisher IDs).

Next steps: I’ll assemble the commercial worksheet, upload sku-matrix-v1.xlsx, and request an intake review for the wk of 20 Jan. Expect a follow-up with a DocuSign MSA link and a short checklist with dependencies.

Meeting scheduled: Tue 13 Jan 10:00 PT (internal sync) — intake review with AWS listing ops proposed for Tue 20 Jan.

Thanks — Priyom
